facts.text: Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) is a standard set of diagram shapes for drawing a safety argument; Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) is a formal data model that lets software tools store and exchange such arguments.
facts.quote: GSN is a standard set of diagram shapes for drawing a safety argument, and SACM is a formal data model that lets software tools store and exchange such arguments.

facts.text: Tim Kelly developed Goal Structuring Notation in the 1990s.
facts.quote: The notation was developed by Tim Kelly in the 1990s

facts.text: The GSN Community Standard version 3 (SCSC-141C, 2021) is identified as the current definition of Goal Structuring Notation.
facts.quote: the GSN Community Standard version 3 (SCSC-141C, 2021) is the current definition.

facts.text: Claims-Arguments-Evidence (CAE) is the main alternative to Goal Structuring Notation and uses the same three ideas with different shapes.
facts.quote: The main alternative, Claims-Arguments-Evidence (CAE), uses the same three ideas with different shapes

facts.text: The Object Management Group's Structured Assurance Case Metamodel defines the data behind an assurance-case diagram rather than a drawing style, allowing arguments to be read across tools and linked to requirement and test databases.
facts.quote: SACM, the Structured Assurance Case Metamodel from the Object Management Group, is not a drawing style but a definition of the data behind one, so an argument built in one tool can be read by another and linked to requirement and test databases.

facts.text: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes what an assurance case must contain.
facts.quote: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 standardizes what an assurance case must contain

facts.text: The booklet recommends a GSN or CAE sketch of the top-level claim in the plan's safety-scope section and a preliminary argument as an appendix.
facts.quote: The booklet recommends a GSN or CAE sketch of the top-level claim in the plan's safety-scope section and a preliminary argument as an appendix

facts.text: The booklet suggests representing the simulation's credibility argument in structured form.
facts.quote: suggests the simulation's credibility argument be represented in structured form

facts.text: The booklet did not find controlled studies of how well readers understand GSN diagrams.
facts.quote: It notes that controlled studies of how well readers understand GSN diagrams were not found

facts.text: An assurance-case drawing is not the safety case, and drawing an argument does not strengthen the underlying evidence.
facts.quote: the caution is that drawing it does not make the evidence underneath any stronger.

facts.text: A shared safety-argument notation lets a safety board, a mining customer and a lawyer read the same argument.
facts.quote: A shared notation lets a safety board, a mining customer and a lawyer read the same argument
